artists.name: Jae Yong Kim
artists.intro: Jae Yong Kim has gained international recognition for his colourful donut ceramic sculptures. The donut, a universally recognizable form, serves as a medium for the artist to incorporate elements from various cultures, including tigers and magpies from Korean folk art, unicorns from Western mythology, and arabesque patterns from the Middle East. These diverse cultural elements, which he has experienced since childhood, blend to symbolise the borderless world of today. Born in Seoul, Kim lives and works in Seoul and New York. He received his BFA in Ceramics & Sculpture from Hartford Art School, University of Hartford, and his MFA in Ceramics from Cranbrook Academy of Art, and has been an Assistant Professor in the Department of Ceramics at Seoul National University of Science & Technology since 2015. His works have been exhibited at institutions including the Powerlong Museum, Shanghai, and the Gwangju Museum of Arts, and are held in public collections such as the Powerlong Museum, the Dennos Museum Center and the University of Hartford.

artists.introZh: 金載容以色彩繽紛的甜甜圈陶瓷雕塑享譽國際。甜甜圈是全世界都能一眼辨識的形狀，藝術家以它為媒介，融入來自各種文化的元素——韓國民畫中的老虎與喜鵲、西方神話中的獨角獸，以及中東的阿拉伯式花紋。這些他自幼年起便接觸的多元文化元素相互交融，象徵著當今無國界的世界。金載容生於首爾，現於首爾與紐約兩地生活與創作。他取得美國哈特福大學哈特福藝術學院陶藝與雕塑學士、克蘭布魯克藝術學院陶藝碩士學位，自2015年起任首爾科學技術大學陶藝系助理教授。其作品曾於上海寶龍美術館、光州市立美術館等機構展出，並為寶龍美術館、丹諾斯博物館中心及哈特福大學等公共機構所典藏。

artists.name: Moon Hyeongtae
artists.intro: Hyeongtae Moon creates a rich world in his paintings that merges expressionist and surrealist ideologies. The influence of CoBRA and Jean Dubuffet can be seen in the childlike distortions, symbolic coding, and warm ochre shades in Moon’s works. The act of repeatedly washing the canvases with water and soil collected from meaningful places in his life, is a signature technique of Moon’s. This unique method, of his, grounds each work in personal memory. The figures in his paintings are simplified yet still somehow expressive. They are often layered with symbolic numbers: 1 for the self, 2 for relationships, 3 for family, 4 for society, and 5 for solitude. Moon’s recent works such as Roof and Merry-Go-Round continue his exploration of intimacy, nostalgia, and the whimsy of everyday life, rendered in bold colors and tactile surfaces that evoke both joy and inner struggle.

artists.introZh: 文亨泰在畫作中構築出一個融合表現主義與超現實主義思想的豐富世界。從他作品中孩童般的變形、符號化的編碼與溫暖的赭色調，可以看見眼鏡蛇畫派（CoBRA）與尚・杜布菲（Jean Dubuffet）的影響。以採集自人生中具有意義之地的水與泥土反覆洗刷畫布，是文亨泰的招牌技法；這種獨特的方法，讓每件作品都紮根於個人的記憶之中。他畫中的人物雖經簡化，卻依然充滿表現力，並常疊上具有象徵意義的數字：1代表自我、2代表關係、3代表家庭、4代表社會、5代表孤獨。〈Roof〉與〈Merry-Go-Round〉等近作延續了他對親密、鄉愁與日常生活奇趣的探索，以大膽的色彩與富觸感的畫面，同時喚起喜悅與內在的掙扎。

artists.name: Yi Yi Jeong-Eun
artists.intro: Yi Yi Jeong-eun vividly captures the myriad of sensations and experiences conveyed by nature with her vibrant brushstrokes on canvas, breathing life into them more powerfully than anyone else. The layers of paint meticulously applied on the canvas capture the beauty of nature through the artist's unique working method. In the early stages of her artistic journey, she focused on themes of consumerism, desires within capitalist society, and the subsequent sense of emptiness. Later, venturing beyond the city, chance encounters with nature led to a transformation in her artistic approach. The vitality and energies inherent in nature, as perceived by the artist's gaze, are expressed through delicate brushstrokes on the canvas. These dynamic artworks allow viewers to keenly feel the emotions Yi Yi Jeong-eun experienced in the heart of nature.

artists.introZh: 異李貞恩以畫布上鮮活的筆觸，生動捕捉自然所傳遞的無數感受與經驗，並以比任何人都更強烈的力量為其注入生命。藝術家以獨特的創作方法，在畫布上一層層細膩堆疊顏料，捕捉自然之美。創作初期，她關注消費主義、資本主義社會中的慾望，以及隨之而來的空虛感；後來走出城市，與自然的偶然相遇，促使她的創作方法產生轉變。透過藝術家的凝視所感知到的自然生命力與能量，化為畫布上細膩的筆觸。這些充滿動感的作品，讓觀者得以深刻感受異李貞恩在大自然懷抱中所經歷的情感。

artists.name: Jin Young
artists.intro: Jin Young, an artist renowned for her anthropomorphized "Piano-Playing Parrot" rendered with deeply evocative colors rooted in traditional Korean painting, captures the essence of contemporary life through her distinctive lens. The "parrot-headed figures" frequently appearing in her works symbolize modern individuals who unconsciously mimic and repeat the actions of others. Jin Young portrays the boundaries of life as islands, yet views the world through the innocent eyes of a child who floats balloons of hope and flies kites within these spaces. Her art reminds us that hope exists here and now, within us, urging us to live fully in the present like children - embracing life with no room for hatred, only love. She emphasizes that even in the repetitive cycles of daily life, the answers to living are clear: the hidden melodies and resonances of life reveal themselves when boundaries dissolve and connections are formed.

artists.introZh: 朴辰英以擬人化的「彈鋼琴的鸚鵡」聞名，運用根植於韓國傳統繪畫、深具感染力的色彩，透過獨特的視角捕捉當代生活的本質。作品中經常出現的「鸚鵡頭人物」，象徵著不自覺地模仿、重複他人行為的現代人。她將生活的邊界描繪成一座座島嶼，卻以孩童般純真的眼光看待世界——在這些空間裡放飛希望的氣球與風箏。她的作品提醒我們，希望就在此時此地、就在我們心中，鼓勵我們像孩子一樣全心活在當下——擁抱生命，心中沒有怨恨，只有愛。她強調，即使在日常生活不斷重複的循環中，生活的答案依然清晰：當邊界消融、連結形成，生命中隱藏的旋律與共鳴便會自然浮現。

artists.name: Choi Hyeji
artists.intro: Choi Hyeji is an artist who tells the story of life and its vibrancy with a particularly unusual medium, cement. Her work captures moments of our lives with vivid colors and matieres that seem to have been created by a child using clay. The artist, who records everything as if it were the feeling of a day viewed through a child's eyes, creates thematic vision by looking at life as the continuation of constant change. In Choi's work, she paints modern people living their daily lives. The people and the impression of themselves to the artist are what she saw when traveling to cities around the world, including New York, Busan, India, and Taipei. Her body of work is represented by the title "LIFE". Painted with cement, her work allows anyone who sees it to reflect their own lives. Although cement in some way has cold properties, it is a medium of potency and vitality that supports the artist's perspective.

artists.introZh: 崔惠智以水泥這種極為特殊的媒材，訴說生命及其蓬勃的活力。她的作品以鮮明的色彩與宛如孩子用黏土捏塑而成的肌理，捕捉我們生活中的片刻。藝術家彷彿以孩童的眼睛感受每一天，記錄下一切，並將生活視為不斷變化的延續，建構出作品的主題視野。崔惠智描繪過著日常生活的現代人——這些人物，以及他們留給藝術家的印象，來自她旅行於紐約、釜山、印度、台北等世界各地城市時的所見所聞。她的系列作品以「LIFE」為題；以水泥繪成的畫面，讓每位觀者都能從中映照出自己的人生。水泥雖在某種程度上帶有冰冷的特質，卻是支撐藝術家觀點、充滿力量與生命力的媒材。

artists.name: Chungshin
artists.intro: Chung Shin draws yellow stills such as tulips and lemons on a well-organized white background with deep charcoal lines to capture the instanteness of the drawing and the visuality of various concepts that are revealed raw. The artist delivers bright and cheerful positive energy to modern people living their busy lives with warm eyes that are everywhere but not seen by anyone. Seeking lines that comfort the heart, the artist says that imagining the coziness of being indoors, moderate splendor, and fruits rolling in the sun arouses the sensation of good feelings. Having done work based on drawings, the artist focuses on revealing through lines the immediacy of drawing as well as the visibility of various concepts that are occasionally revealed raw. Through a warm gaze, ubiquitous but not visible to everyone, the artist attempts to convey a bright and cheerful energy to modern people living busy everyday lives.

artists.introZh: 金青信在整潔的白色背景上，以深沉的炭筆線條描繪鬱金香、檸檬等黃色靜物，捕捉素描的即時性，以及各種概念赤裸呈現時的視覺性。藝術家以無所不在、卻不為任何人所見的溫暖目光，為忙碌生活中的現代人傳遞明亮、愉快的正向能量。她追尋能撫慰人心的線條，並表示：想像待在室內的舒適、恰到好處的華麗，以及在陽光下滾動的水果，便會喚起美好的感受。以素描為創作基礎的她，專注於透過線條呈現素描的直接性，以及偶爾赤裸顯露的各種概念的可見性。藉由這份無所不在、卻並非人人都能看見的溫暖凝視，藝術家試圖將明亮而愉快的能量，傳遞給過著忙碌日常的現代人。

artists.name: Lee Anon
artists.intro: Lee Anon visualizes fictitious stages where “albino” animals, those who are short of melanin pigments, live in the midst of tranquil and mysterious forest. Being white, albinos are vulnerable to predators as they are easily exposed. Despite this, they live along harmoniously taking care of each other. This is an expression of solidarity and declaration to step forward with all the albinos in the world who acknowledged their existence as well as uncertainties and finiteness of earthly lives. The matiere, layered intensively, is a metaphor to the artist’s wish to embrace all fragile lives and to protect the warmth of our world. Lee Anon is rapidly gaining critical acclaim for idiosyncratic style of portraying mysterious forests where albino animals inhabit.

artists.introZh: 李安穩描繪出一個個虛構的舞台：缺乏黑色素的「白化」動物，生活在寧靜而神祕的森林之中。白化動物因通體雪白，容易暴露行蹤而易受掠食者攻擊；儘管如此，牠們仍彼此照顧、和諧共生。這是一種團結的表達，也是一份宣言——與世界上所有承認自身存在、也接受塵世生命之不確定與有限的白化生命一同向前邁進。層層密集堆疊的肌理，隱喻著藝術家想擁抱所有脆弱生命、守護這個世界溫度的心願。李安穩以描繪白化動物棲居於神祕森林的獨特風格，正迅速獲得藝評界的肯定。

artists.name: Im Hari
artists.intro: Im Hari (b. 1994) channels the private emotions of pregnancy, childbirth, and early motherhood into paintings built around 'Furry Bread,' an imaginary creature of her own invention. More interested in the moment of becoming than in any finished form, she lets airbrushed atmosphere and brushed texture trade places, deliberately leaving the creature's outline soft and unresolved. Pink-purple and turquoise sit against pastel and deep shadow, while stars, petals, and drops of water drift through the scene, turning the canvas into a psychological space where feeling floats free. Her steady affirmation of imperfection and change offers a quiet, comforting presence.

artists.introZh: 任hari（1994年生）將懷孕、分娩與初為人母的私密情感，化為以她自創的想像生物「毛茸茸麵包（Furry Bread）」為核心的繪畫。比起任何完成的形態，她更關注「正在成為」的瞬間，讓噴槍營造的氛圍與筆刷的肌理彼此交替，刻意使生物的輪廓保持柔和、未定。粉紫與土耳其藍置於粉彩色調與深沉陰影之間，星星、花瓣與水滴在畫面中飄浮，使畫布成為情感得以自由漂浮的心理空間。她對不完美與變化始終如一的肯定，帶來一種安靜而撫慰人心的存在感。

artists.name: Lee Yelin
artists.intro: Yelin Lee paints expressionless girls drawn from the visual memory of childhood comics and anime, fixing the fleeting spontaneity of a digital sketch into the lasting materiality of layered acrylic. Rather than depicting a specific person, she builds an anonymous figure who is at once herself and not herself; the girl's frontal gaze meets the viewer's own, holding purity and unease, fracture and resilience together, until the image comes to stand for anyone who has occupied a vulnerable place.

artists.introZh: 李藝璘描繪源自童年漫畫與動畫視覺記憶的無表情少女，將數位草圖稍縱即逝的即興感，固定為層層壓克力顏料所構成的持久物質性。她並非描繪某個特定的人，而是塑造一個既是自己、又不是自己的匿名人物；少女正面的凝視迎向觀者的目光，同時承載著純真與不安、破碎與韌性，直到這個形象最終代表了每一個曾身處脆弱位置的人。

artists.name: Yuya Hashizume
artists.intro: Yuya Hashizume rose to fame for his Eyewater series, a collection of paintings in which a person is depicted against a monochrome background using the technique of Japanese manga and with a single tear falling from one eye, and is gaining attention in Japan as well as throughout Asia and Europe. Having been interested in drawing and making things with his hands since childhood, Hashizume worked for several years at an outdoor clothing brand after graduating from university, during which time he learned the basics of branding and product design. After several more career experiences, including designing advertisements and other promotional materials, Hashizume eventually developed a signature style that culminated in his first solo exhibition, "eyewater," in 2017 at Tokyo's Classic Bowl, which was warmly received by the global art community. Hashizume's creations are inverse depictions of modern social phenomena that the artist is interested in, such as loss of originality or the tendency for unique things to be quickly shared among many. His artistic world is made up of paintings of people and animals that reflect the style of Fujiko F. Fujio, the writer and illustrator of Doraemon, a manga series that instilled in the young Hashizume the concepts of artificiality and anonymity.

artists.introZh: 橋爪悠也以「Eyewater」系列成名——畫中人物以日本漫畫的手法描繪於單色背景前，一隻眼睛落下一滴淚——不僅在日本，在亞洲與歐洲各地也備受矚目。橋爪自幼便喜歡畫畫與動手製作，大學畢業後在一家戶外服飾品牌工作數年，期間習得品牌經營與產品設計的基礎。之後他又累積了設計廣告與各類宣傳品等多種職涯經驗，逐漸發展出個人的招牌風格，並於2017年在東京Classic Bowl舉辦首次個展「eyewater」，獲得國際藝術圈的熱烈迴響。橋爪的創作，是對他所關注之現代社會現象——例如原創性的喪失，或獨特事物迅速被大眾分享的趨勢——的反向描繪。他的藝術世界由人物與動物的畫作構成，反映出《哆啦A夢》作者藤子・F・不二雄的風格；這部漫畫在橋爪年少時，為他種下了「人工性」與「匿名性」的概念。
